+title: Port StdioServerProcess onto the shared ProcessRegistry
+---
+## What
+Port the stdio transport that eventplan.md § "Consolidation of the siblings" names (`StdioServerProcess`). Behavioral port; new header comments in the `//` block style of `Capabilities/Shell/ShellCapability.swift`.
+
+- Source: `/Users/wballard/github/swissarmyhammer/FoundationModelsMCP/Sources/FoundationModelsMCP/StdioServerProcess.swift` (814 lines).
+- Target: `Sources/FoundationModelsMultitool/Capabilities/MCP/StdioServerProcess.swift`.
+- The source has its own `ProcessRegistry.swift`. Do NOT port it. This package uses the shared `FoundationModelsExtras.ProcessRegistry` (see the `extrasDependencyName` comment in `Package.swift` and `Capabilities/Shell/ShellRunner.swift`). Register each spawned server process into `ProcessRegistry.global`, the way `ShellRunner` does, so the `atexit` sweep reaches it.
+- eventplan.md: "Server subprocesses are infrastructure. They have session lifetime, they are never runs, and they never get a `completionToken`." State this in the header. `shutdown()` and `respawn()` stay as they are.
+- Keep `StdioServerProcess` public: a host constructs it to name the server command. Keep the transport factory shape (`respawn() -> any Transport`), because the server task connects through a `TransportFactory`.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] A server command spawns, its transport carries an `initialize` round trip, and `shutdown()` ends the process group.
+- [ ] Each spawned process is in `ProcessRegistry.global` while it runs, and it is gone after `shutdown()`.
+- [ ] No second `ProcessRegistry` type exists in this package.
+- [ ] `swift build` succeeds.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] Port `StdioServerProcessTests.swift` from `/Users/wballard/github/swissarmyhammer/FoundationModelsMCP/Tests/FoundationModelsMCPTests/` into `Tests/FoundationModelsMultitoolTests/`. Replace the source's registry assertions with assertions against `FoundationModelsExtras.ProcessRegistry`. Cases that need the `mcp-test-server` executable wait for the test-server task; list them in the header and port them there.
+- [ ] `swift test --filter StdioServerProcessTests` passes.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — port the tests first, then port the code to make them pass. #eventplan #phase-4
\ No newline at end of file

+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m11p947m8azem4d0chkjtb6w
+  text: |-
+    Research and decisions of the port:
+
+    - The source defines `TransportFactory`, `NonRetryableConnectError` and `DisposableTransport` in `MCPServer.swift`. `MCPServer` comes in task ^832pg8r, and `StdioServerProcess` conforms to the two protocols. So the two protocols stand in a new file `Capabilities/MCP/TransportContracts.swift` (internal). The `TransportFactory` alias is NOT added: nothing reads it yet, and an unread alias is dead code. The MCPServer task adds it.
+    - The sdk's `Transport` protocol requires `var logger: Logging.Logger`. The wrapper actor must name that type to conform, so `StdioServerProcess.swift` carries `import Logging`. It logs nothing through it. `swift build` accepts the import with no product declared (verified with a probe file, then removed). The `Package.swift` comment on `mcpPackage` and the `MCPCapability.swift` header now say this; the manifest still declares no `swift-log` product.
+    - Four tests of the source connect an `MCPServer` over the transport, and two also spawn `mcp-test-server`. They are not portable yet. The header of the test file lists them by name, with the task each one waits for (^832pg8r, ^gqrtxxy).
+    - The group-kill test of the source counted process-group members with `pgrep -g`. The port asserts by pid instead: the script prints `$!` of each backgrounded `sleep`, and the test reads the pids off the transport, then polls `kill(pid, 0)` for `ESRCH` with `TestPoll.holds`.
+    - The owner-teardown test failed on the first run: a `guard let held = stdio` made a second strong copy of the value, and the `deinit` did not fire. The spawn and the pid read now happen in a helper that takes the optional, so no copy outlives the `stdio = nil`.
+    - One test spawns through the public initializer and reads `ProcessRegistry.global` (no sweep) to prove the registration into the global table.
+
+    `swift build --build-tests` is clean, and `swift test --filter StdioServerProcessTests` passes 16 tests.
